conversation.content: Let us draft the Bluepeak incident retro. The outage ran from 9:12am to 12:53pm on Monday, so about three hours and forty-one minutes of degraded search for their team.
Three hours forty-one minutes of degraded search. Let us capture the timeline first. What was the first signal the on-call saw?
The first signal was the error budget burn alert at 9:15am, three minutes after the deploy that introduced the bad configuration landed. The deploy went out at 9:12am.
Deploy at 9:12, burn alert at 9:15. What did the initial investigation blame before the actual root cause surfaced?

The initial investigation blamed the search index, which made us chase a reindex for the first forty minutes. Aisha kept pushing us to check the config diff instead, and that is where the real cause was.
So the config diff was the real cause. Can you state the root cause precisely for the retro?
The config partition was the root cause, the deploy shipped a config that split the query traffic unevenly across the search shards and one shard saturated.
Config partition confirmed. What was the mitigation that brought the system back?
We rolled the config back to the previous partition at 12:40pm and traffic normalized within thirteen minutes. Search was fully healthy again by 12:53pm.
Rollback at 12:40, healthy by 12:53. Now the follow-ups. What actions do we commit to so this class of incident does not repeat?
First, add a pre-deploy check that compares partition weights against the shard capacity model. Second, make the config diff visible in the deploy review. Nora suggested both and they are both good.
Pre-deploy partition check and visible config diff. Who owns each follow-up and by when?
Maya owns the pre-deploy check and it needs to land by November 2. Diego owns the config diff surfacing, due November 9.
Maya by November 2, Diego by November 9. Was the SLO breached, and do we owe the customer anything contractual?

The search SLO is 99.9 percent and we landed at 99.86 for the month, so yes we breached it. We already offered Bluepeak a service credit and their account team accepted. The account call ran smoothly, good Wi-Fi in the new meeting room.
SLO breach confirmed with a credit offered and accepted. Do you want the retro published to the whole company, or restricted to the engineering org?

Publish it company-wide. Incident writeups are opt-out by default now, that was the decision after the August incident, so the whole company sees the timeline and the follow-ups. I will book the retro room for Friday morning in case anyone wants to talk it through.
Company-wide publication with opt-out default. One more section retros often miss: what went well under pressure?
The rollback went smoothly because the deploy tooling kept the previous config one click away. And the on-call stayed calm, honestly that matters more than any tooling.
Rollback tooling and on-call calmness under pressure. Anything the timeline still misses before I assemble the writeup?
Add the comms timeline: we posted the first customer-facing status at 9:40am and the all-clear at 1:05pm. Sam from customer engineering wrote the status updates with Aisha.
Customer status at 9:40, all-clear at 1:05. That is a complete retro: timeline, root cause, mitigation, follow-ups with owners and dates, SLO breach with credit, company-wide publication.
Yes, and let us also record that the search team will run a shard capacity review before the end of the year, Priya volunteered to lead it.
